description: Migrate all folders from source to target, preserving full hierarchy.

action.description: Conflict strategy applied to every folder.

concurrency.description: Same as in ``migrate_folders`` — maximum number of folders to create/delete concurrently within each hierarchy depth level.

examples.user_query: Migrate all folders, skipping any that already exist.
examples.notes: This call migrates all folders from the source to the target environment, preserving the folder hierarchy. Existing folders in the target environment are skipped.

examples.user_query: How can I migrate all folders and overwrite any existing ones in the target environment?
examples.notes: This call migrates all folders from the source to the target environment, preserving the folder hierarchy. Any existing folders in the target environment are overwritten.

examples.user_query: Migrate all folders and duplicate any that already exist, using a concurrency level of 5.
examples.notes: This call migrates all folders from the source to the target environment, preserving the folder hierarchy. Existing folders in the target environment are duplicated, and up to 5 folders are processed concurrently at each hierarchy depth level.

description: Migrate specific folders and their full subtrees from source to target.

folder_ids.description: Folder OIDs to migrate. Provide either this or ``folder_names``.

folder_names.description: Folder display names to migrate. Provide either this or ``folder_ids``.

action.description: Conflict strategy when a folder at the same path already exists on the target. - ``"skip"`` — leave the existing folder unchanged and map its OID so child folders can still be placed under it correctly. - ``"overwrite"`` — delete the existing folder then recreate from source. **Warning:** deleting a folder on Sisense also removes all dashboards inside it. - ``"duplicate"`` — always create, regardless of conflicts.

concurrency.description: Maximum number of folders to create/delete concurrently within each hierarchy depth level, run via a background thread pool (``asyncio.to_thread``) since the underlying HTTP client is synchronous. Folders at the same depth are independent — their parent was already migrated in an earlier, fully-completed depth level — so they're safe to run in parallel; different depths are still processed strictly in order, since a child's target parent OID must exist before it can be created. Values <= 1 (the default) process folders one at a time.

examples.user_query: Migrate all dashboards, skipping any that already exist.
examples.notes: This call migrates the specified folders and their subtrees from the source to the target, skipping any folders that already exist on the target.

examples.user_query: How can I duplicate the folders named 'Sales Reports' and 'Marketing Data' to a new environment?
examples.notes: This call duplicates the specified folders by name, ensuring that conflicts do not overwrite or skip existing folders on the target.

examples.user_query: Overwrite the folders with IDs 'xyz789' and 'ghi012' in the target environment, processing them concurrently.
examples.notes: This call overwrites the specified folders by ID, recreating them on the target environment and processing up to 5 folders concurrently at each hierarchy depth.
